articles.title: Jasprit Bumrah, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on Afghanistan's radar: Ibrahim Zadran reveals plans
articles.summary: Cricket News: Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran says his team has made specific plans to deal with Jasprit Bumrah in Sunday's opening T20I against India at the Aru.
articles.body: Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran says his team has made specific plans to deal with Jasprit Bumrah in Sunday's opening T20I against India at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi.Bumrah is set to return to international cricket after missing matches due to a left knee injury. His return gives India another major option with the ball, but Zadran said Afghanistan will not make things complicated while facing the star pacer."If you look at Jasprit Bumrah, he is one of the best, and he is my favourite fast bowler. We as a group never think things in a complicated way for ourselves. So we have a very good plan for him, and we just thought about him, how to play against him, and hopefully we are going to play better cricket against Jasprit Bumrah or the Indian Cricket Team," Zadran told reporters in a press conference on Saturday.Sooryavanshi also on Afghanistan's radarAfghanistan have also prepared for India's teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.The Afghanistan team has used information from players who have faced the left-handed opener in the IPL. Zadran said they have also studied videos of Sooryavanshi before the series."He is an amazing talent. Recently, he played great cricket in the Indian Premier League (IPL), and he has been performing well at a different level in cricket events. We have thought about him, and we have gained that knowledge from those guys who have played against him in the IPL.“We have already watched his videos, and we just try to keep it very simple for ourselves, just to execute the right plans at the right time against him. We are just trying to make things simple for us, not complicated," he stated.Zadran takes over T20I captaincyZadran has taken over the T20I captaincy from Rashid Khan. He believes their strong relationship will help Afghanistan make a fresh start after their early exit from the T20 World Cup.The new captain also feels Afghanistan's experience of playing in India will be useful."I would say, I was destined to have a captain like Rashid Khan. Alongside him, we had better communication, better understanding between us. When he was a captain, I was helping him as a vice-captain, and the understanding is there.“Yes, we have played enough cricket here in India; we all know the conditions, how to play, how to adjust ourselves, and we have played a series here against India, and the T20 World Cup, and the 50-over World Cup as well. We know the conditions really well, and how to play. We just need to execute the plan really well, according to the opposition, and that's it."Afghanistan eye first series win over IndiaAfghanistan are yet to beat India in a bilateral T20I series and Zadran is hoping his side can change that this time.He said the key will be to execute their plans properly and focus on the process instead of worrying about the result."Yes, we have played better cricket against India. In 2024, we had two super overs against them in the T20I series in Bengaluru.“At the ICC events, we have played better cricket against them. As you mentioned, we have never beaten them. Hopefully, we are going to play a good series, win a game, and win a series from them. But it's all about execution of the plan and giving your 100 percent.“It’s about trying to make things easy for ourselves, not complicated. Yes, we just try to give 100 percent. Don't think about the result; just try to think about the process, and how we are going to deliver. I am sure we will have a better series."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We need to sit down and reflect on our mistakes’: Babar Azam calls for changes after Pakistan’s 0-3 England sweep
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has called for an honest assessment of the team's mistakes and selection strategy after England completed a 3-0 Test serie.
articles.body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has called for an honest assessment of the team's mistakes and selection strategy after England completed a 3-0 Test series sweep with an eight-wicket victory at Edgbaston on Saturday.Babar admitted Pakistan now need to reassess their personnel and decide on their best playing XI after a difficult tour in which the visitors struggled to adapt to English conditions. He said the team management, selectors and captain would need to sit together and determine the way forward.“I think we need to sit down and reflect on our mistakes, decide what type of playing eleven, and decide our players. I think they are sitting, and the manager is coming, the selector is coming, and I sit back and then decide our best eleven,” Babar said after the defeat.The series ended with Pakistan's batting showing signs of improvement in Birmingham. After being bowled out for under 200 in both innings of the opening two Tests, they posted 449 in their second innings at Edgbaston to set England a target of 130.‘Unfortunately, we have a couple of changes after losing two matches’Debutant Razaullah provided the biggest spark for Pakistan, making an immediate impact with both bat and ball. He took four wickets in England's first innings before smashing 81 off 63 balls, including nine sixes.Shan Masood scored 95, Babar contributed 76 and opener Azam Awais made 59 as Pakistan finally offered substantial resistance with the bat.Mohammad Abbas then gave the visitors a glimmer of hope by removing two England batters in the opening over of England's chase. Babar admitted Pakistan briefly believed they could force an unlikely result before Joe Root and Jordan Cox took control.“Yes. We took two wickets in the first over. So we believe high, always high. But I think Root and both batsmen playing are very good,” he said.Root finished unbeaten on 62 and Cox scored 59, with their unbroken 128-run partnership taking England to victory.Reflecting on Pakistan's selection throughout the series, Babar described the changes made after the first two defeats as unfortunate, while also pointing to the difficulty of batting in the conditions.“Before we come here, we think about different things, and then we decide our team. And then unfortunately, we have a couple of changes after losing two matches because when we are coming to England, it is very difficult for the batsmen, and the first two pitches are very difficult,” he said.Babar backs Razaullah after breakthrough TestWhile Pakistan leave England with plenty to reconsider, Razaullah's performance offered a major positive. Despite his limited first-class experience, the youngster made an immediate impression on Test debut.“We enjoyed it. I think everyone is enjoying his innings and bowling, and he is a very good talent and raw. I think he’s good for us. The way he played this match and he’s giving confidence,” Babar said.The captain also stressed the importance of giving young players opportunities while adapting the team's approach according to conditions.“When you’re coming to different series, you try to do your best, and you decide what type of cricket to play in different conditions. I think these conditions are difficult, but I think we try to get all the new boys to utilise their talent in here,” he said.The 3-0 defeat leaves Pakistan at the bottom of the World Test Championship standings. articles.title: Game time after injury hiccups: Full-strength India take on Afghanistan in first T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: It has been a rough initiation into the T20I captaincy for Shreyas Iyer, having returned winless from the tour of Ireland and England in Ju.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It has been a rough initiation into the T20I captaincy for Shreyas Iyer, having returned winless from the tour of Ireland and England in June-July. However, the first T20I against Afghanistan here on Sunday will be the first time he can boast of having a first-choice team to work with.Iyer’s captaincy came in bizarre circumstances after the selectors decided to unceremoniously dump T20 World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav. Ever since, Indian cricket has been beset with injury problems, with the BCCI even inviting Iyer for a crucial review meeting earlier this month.“It (injuries to players) is not frustrating. We need to understand the amount of matches a player is playing continuously. He’s bound to get injured some way or the other because the intensity is pretty high,” Iyer said. “Of course, it certainly impacts the combination. All you can control is whoever is available on that given day, and we need to give that sort of confidence to that particular player. A backup is equally important for the team. We know they can deliver as well,” he added.This will also be the first time Iyer will have the services of pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, who is coming off a long layoff. “As a player comes out of injury, it’s important that he gets more game time. Bumrah has played so much cricket over the years. He is well experienced,” Iyer said.Iyer says team excited to interact with Olympic athletesThis three-match series, in essence, is a warmup before India fly out to Japan for the Asian Games on Sept 19. Iyer said the team would be excited to spend time with athletes from other disciplines.“It is definitely an exciting time for me. It’s going to be my first time (at a multi-sports event). There are a couple of players who have already been at the last Asian Games. The first match we are going to play is against Japan, so that is going to be a historic one. Sharing a relationship with the hockey players and other Olympic players is exciting. We will definitely go and cheer our athletes whenever we get time,” Iyer said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Cricket News: It will be spin versus spin in the title clash of the 2026 Women’s Asia Cup. On slow Dubai pitches where spinners have dominated, seven-time champions.
articles.body: It will be spin versus spin in the title clash of the 2026 Women’s Asia Cup. On slow Dubai pitches where spinners have dominated, seven-time champions India will rely on senior allrounder Deepti Sharma and explosive openers Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma when they take on a resilient Sri Lanka in Sunday’s T20 Asia Cup final at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.The ball has largely dominated the bat in this edition. India’s spinners have taken 26 wickets in four matches, while Sri Lanka’s tweakers have 25. Shafali has defied those conditions, emerging as the tournament’s leading run-scorer with 168 runs at a strike rate of 169.69 and an average of 42.00. Mandhana has scored 154 at 38.50, striking at 171.11.The two sides’ premier off-spinning allrounders, Deepti and Sri Lanka skipper Chamari Athapaththu, are joint leading wicket-takers with 11 scalps each. Deepti, the fulcrum of India’s attack, followed a six-ball 13 in the semifinal against Bangladesh with 3-26 to help India defend 149.With economical left-arm spinner Shree Charani, India’s leading T20I wicket-taker in 2026, and impressive leg-spinner Prema Rawat alongside Deepti, India have a potent spin attack for the Dubai conditions. Deepti is now the leading wicket-taker in T20Is, with 179 wickets in 153 matches.Both teams are unbeaten, having won all four matches. India, however, will be keen to avenge Sri Lanka’s stunning eight-wicket win in the 2024 final in Dambulla, when Harshitha Samarawickrama (69*) and Athapaththu (61) powered the hosts to a comfortable chase of 166.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Diamondbacks 2, Texas 6: Return of the One Big Inning
articles.summary: At least Tim Tawa got his first major league triple, and Pavin Smith had an RBI!
articles.body:
Well, you know what they say: "You can't win 'em all." On paper, it looked like maybe we should have won this one, and if you were keeping score, it would not have been lost at you that we basically won eight out of the nine innings that were played tonight. Sadly, however, that's not how baseball works. Early in the season, before his forced vacation in Reno, we became very familiar with Brandon Pfaadt , tonight's starter, pitching at least okay for a handful of innings and then having there be the One Big Inning™ where everything kinda blew up. Upon Brandon's return, we still saw some of that, except that the offending innings were generally pretty mild—one or two or three runs at most, which kept things close enough that we could get back into it. But that was not the case tonight.

He was going up against former first-round draft pick and general underperformer Kumar Rocker , and in terms of the numbers, it was a very favorable matchup. Rocker is often wild, and throws a bunch of pitches, and gives up a lot of walks, and leaves ballgames a lot earlier than you tend to want your starter to leave. Irritatingly, though, he was quite efficient in the early going tonight, as he and Pfaadt traded quick, scoreless innings in the first and second. After two innings, Rocker had thrown 24 pitches; Pfaadt, despite having given up two hits to Rocker's none, had only thrown 23. Pfaadt had another shutdown inning in the top of the third, adding only 12 more pitches to his count and setting down the Rangers in order, and Tim Tawa led off the bottom of the third with a triple off the wall in pretty much straightaway center field:

Pavin Smith , who was for many of us a surprise call-up from Reno today, then grounded a single past Corey Seager and into left field to drive in Timmy. Three quick outs followed, but we'd drawn first blood against Rocker and that Rangers. 1-0 DBACKS

Pfaadt recorded another 1-2-3 inning in the top of the fourth, we sat down in order against Rocker in the bottom half, and then the fifth inning rolled around, much like a giant stone boulder bearing down a steep slope in a narrow passageway, heading straight for our guy. And alas, Brandon Pfgaadt was no Indiana Jones; he couldn't get out of the way.

It started with a leadoff dinger by Wyatt Langford to tie the game, and was followed by a single, a stoledn abse, a sacrifice bunt, another single that scored a run, a hit by pitch. and then a fielder's choice that looked like an inning-ending double play but which was overturned by a review that determined that Brandon Pfaadt's foot was perhaps not on the bag when he ran over to cover first base. The call on the field was "safe," and while the replays we saw on the broadcast really looked like they'd be enough to overturn that call, but it was not to be, and the call stood. That completely knocked Pfaadt off kilter, and the next three batters went single-double-single before he finally struck out Wyatt Langford, the tenth batter of the inning, to put it to bed. 6-1 Texas

And that was pretty much that. Somewhat surprisingly, Pfaadt came out and pitched the sixth, and he even recorded the first two outs in the seventh, and it was all good and all zeros, but the damage had been done.

Kumar Rocker, meanwhile, walked Nolan Arenado and Tim Tawa to lead off the bottom of the fifth, and that ended his night, and Texas got their bullpen involved and that bullpen also proved to be irritatingly effective. Both of the leadoff walks were left stranded. Rangers' opening day starter Nathan Eovaldi , fresh off the IL and returning to big league action without any rehab starts or anything, let us get a second run in the bottom of the sixth, thanks to one-out singles by Gabriel Moreno and Geraldo Perdomo , followed by a Corbin Carroll sacrifice fly that scored Moreno from third, which narrowed the game to 6-2 Texas

But that was where it stayed. Jonathan Loaisiga , Derek Law , and Juan Morillo put zeroes up the rest of the way for us, but there was nothing further doing from the offense, despite us putting the leadoff runners on in both the seventh and eighth innings. And so it was. 6-2 Texas FINAL

Loss Probability Added, courtesy of FanGraphs

The Lost Ark: Nobody . The Last Crusade: Tim Tawa (3 AB, 1 H, 1 R, 1 3B, 1 BB, +10% WPA) The Crystal Skull: Brandon Pfaadt (6 2/3 IP, 10 H, 6 R, 6 ER, 0 BB, 7 K, 1 HR, -34% WPA)

It was a fairly sparse Gameday Thread this evening, with 201 comments at time of writing. Precious few recs got handed out tonight as well, and pretty much the only comments to go Sedona Red were concentrated at the start of the game, when folks were still marveling at the return of Pavin Smith to a major league roster and a starting lineup. As such, tonight's Comment of the Game goes to onedotfive, for this solid suggestion about how we might find a way to turn his presence to our collective advantage in the remaining days of the season:

Works for me….I think Baxter is creepy anyway.

So join us tomorrow afternoon for the rubber match of the series. Hologram Eddie takes the mound for us; Cal Quantrill goes for Texas. First pitch is scheduled for 1:10pm AZ time. Hope to see you around the place!

As always, thanks for reading, and as always, go Diamondbacks !

articles.title: Will India accept the Women's Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi? Exploring possible boycott of Pakistan's ACC and PCB chief
articles.summary: With Pakistan Cricket Board Chief Mohsin Naqvi set to present the Asia Cup to the winning team, here's if Team India Women will accept the trophy from him.
articles.body:
The Men's Asia Cup trophy still has not been handed over to India after the September 2025 final.

Mohsin Naqvi is expected to attend the Women's Asia Cup final in Dubai on September 13.

India's men refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi, who is also Pakistan's interior minister.

Will India accept the Women's Asia Cup trophy from Mohsin Naqvi?

India's women are the side to be defeated at the 2026 Asia Cup and the clear favourites to reach the final on September 13. However, one question remains that has nothing to do with cricket. If Harmanpreet Kaur's team lifts the trophy, who will hand it to them?

Under normal circumstances, the answer would be the president of the Asian Cricket Council. That happens to be Mohsin Naqvi, who is simultaneously the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and the interior minister of Pakistan, a combination of roles that caused a full-blown diplomatic incident the last time he tried to present a trophy to an Indian side.

Journalist Rohit Jaglan of Rezsports flagged the issue ahead of the group stage, noting that Naqvi was not present for the Women's Asia Cup trophy unveiling ceremony but had attended the corresponding men's event. His absence from the unveiling does not guarantee his absence from the final.

Who is Mohsin Naqvi, and why would he present the Women's Asia Cup trophy?

Naqvi was elected ACC president for a two-year term in April 2025, succeeding Sri Lanka's Shammi Silva. He holds the position alongside his PCB chairmanship and his cabinet portfolio as Pakistan's interior minister, a combination that has made him arguably the most politically prominent figure in Asian cricket administration.

His path to the cricket establishment began through politics rather than the sport itself. Naqvi served as caretaker chief minister of Punjab province from January 2023 to February 2024, and his appointment to the PCB came without a professional cricketing background.

He has since consolidated his position, with PCB-backed candidates sweeping all three contested ACC board seats at the Bangkok AGM in August 2026.

As ACC president, it is his prerogative to present the trophy at the continental body's flagship events. He did so at the Men's Asia Cup final in September 2025, or at least attempted to, and was listed in the ACC's official pre-tournament communication as the individual who would hand over the silverware to the winners.

What happened when India's men's team refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi?

India beat Pakistan by five wickets in a thrilling final-over finish at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on September 28, 2025. What followed was one of the most extraordinary episodes in Asian cricket's history.

The presentation ceremony was delayed by more than an hour after the match ended. While the match finished at around 10:30 PM Dubai time, the wait stretched to close to midnight. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia confirmed what had caused the hold-up.

"We have decided not to take the Asia Cup trophy from the ACC chairman, who happens to be one of the main political leaders of Pakistan," Saikia told ANI. "So we decided not to take it from him."

India's players had reportedly indicated they were willing to accept the trophy from Emirates Cricket Board vice-chairman Khalid Al Zarooni instead, but that request was denied. Eventually, an official quietly removed the trophy from the dais and carried it off the field without explanation.

Suryakumar Yadav's team celebrated their victory without the physical trophy, posing for photographs miming the act of holding it. The standoff reflected the broader political tensions between the two countries following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, which had already seen India refuse to shake hands with Pakistan players across all three meetings during the tournament.

The trophy still had not reached the BCCI by early November. Saikia wrote to the ACC requesting its handover, and when Naqvi refused to release it, the BCCI threatened to raise the matter at the ICC meeting on November 4. Naqvi denied having apologised and instead invited India to collect the trophy from the ACC office in Dubai.

Will India captain, Harmanpreet Kaur, accept the trophy if they win the Women's Asia Cup?

No official position has been stated by the BCCI on the women's tournament, and the question has not been put directly to Harmanpreet Kaur or the team management. It is, however, impossible to separate it from the unresolved men's trophy standoff.

There are three possible outcomes if India reaches the final and wins. The first is that Naqvi presents the trophy and India accepts it, which would represent a climbdown from the position Saikia articulated in September and seems unlikely given the men's trophy dispute remains open.

The second is a repeat of the men's scenario, with India refusing and the ceremony descending into another standoff at the same venue. The third, and perhaps likeliest, is that the ACC quietly arranges for a different dignitary to handle the presentation, avoiding the confrontation entirely.

Naqvi's absence from the trophy unveiling ceremony may hint at this kind of behind-the-scenes arrangement, though nothing has been confirmed. What is certain is that this is not a decision the players will make on their own.

If the men's episode demonstrated anything, it was that the instruction came from the BCCI rather than the dressing room, and any directive for the women's final will follow the same chain. The players will play the cricket, the board will handle the politics, and whether the trophy ends up in their hands or in the ACC office will be determined well above Harmanpreet Kaur's pay grade.

articles.title: 'Probs will go to a pub': Ben Stokes posts cheeky Instagram story as team secure promotion in County
articles.summary: Cricket News: Ben Stokes shared a cheeky Instagram story after his Country team Durham secured promotion to Division One of the England's County Championship.Stokes.
articles.body: Ben Stokes shared a cheeky Instagram story after his Country team Durham secured promotion to Division One of the England's County Championship.Stokes missed the latest round of the Championship, but posted on Instagram after Durham’s win over Middlesex guaranteed them top spot in Division Two. “Probs will go to a pub,” he wrote. “Save yourself the effort of sending smart arse replies to my previous story.”Stokes, who retired from international cricket after the New Zealand Test series, was filmed leaving a nightclub in August while his Durham teammate Brydon Carse was being handcuffed by police. He was also involved in another nightclub episode in Bristol in June with Gus Atkinson and missed The Oval Test against New Zealand after an ECB disciplinary probe.Durham return to Division OneDurham were relegated to Division Two in 2025 after winning only two of their 14 matches in the top tier. They responded in 2026 by going unbeaten in 12 matches in the ongoing Division Two season and securing top spot with 230 points, 55 more than second-placed Northamptonshire, with two matches still to play.Their 93-run win over Middlesex confirmed their promotion, Wisden reported. Brydon Carse took nine wickets in the match, while Ben McKinney’s 184 helped Durham move towards victory.Durham are now on a six-match winning run. They have beaten Derbyshire and Northamptonshire twice each and Gloucestershire and Middlesex once during that run.Durham will play Worcestershire and Lancashire in their remaining two fixtures, starting on September 15 and September 24 respectively.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
